An interface with its members in no particular order is hard to scan, and two branches that each add a member at the end conflict. This rule keeps the members of every `interface` in alphabetical order, ignoring case. Properties, methods and index signatures are sorted together, by name. A call signature, `(): void`, or a construct signature, `new (): T`, splits the interface: the members before and after it are sorted on their own. `--fix` reorders the members, and each one takes the comment above it along.

The same for `type X = { .. }` is [`perfectionist/sort-object-types`](/lint/rules/perfectionist/sort-object-types).

{/* Generated by src/codegen/lint-rule-docs.ts. Do not edit this section. */}

## Configure

Off by default. To turn it on:

```toml bunfig.toml
[lint.rules]
"perfectionist/sort-interfaces" = "error" # or "warn"
```

Every option, set to its default. The ones that are commented out are unset by default.

```toml bunfig.toml
[lint.rules]
"perfectionist/sort-interfaces" = ["error", {
  type = "alphabetical",
  order = "asc", # "asc" or "desc"
  ignoreCase = true,
  specialCharacters = "keep", # "remove", "trim" or "keep"
  alphabet = "", # string
  locales = "en-US",
  sortBy = "name", # "name" or "value"
  fallbackSort = {
    type = "unsorted",
    # order = <"asc" or "desc">,
    sortBy = "name", # "name" or "value"
  },
  groups = [],
  customGroups = [], # list of objects
  newlinesBetween = "ignore", # "ignore" or number
  newlinesInside = "newlinesBetween", # "ignore", number or "newlinesBetween"
  partitionByNewLine = false,
  partitionByComment = false,
  useConfigurationIf = {
    # allNamesMatchPattern = <list of objects or strings, object or string>,
    # hasNumericKeysOnly = <true or false>,
    # declarationCommentMatchesPattern = <list, object or string>,
    # matchesAstSelector = <string>,
    # declarationMatchesPattern = <list, object or string>,
  },
}]
```

{/* End of the generated section. */}

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad */}
```ts
interface User {
  name: string;
  id: number;
  email?: string;
}
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}
```ts
interface User {
  email?: string;
  id: number;
  name: string;
}
```

## Options

The rule takes one or more configuration objects. With more than one, the first whose `useConfigurationIf` matches the interface applies to it.

| Option | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `type` | `"alphabetical"` | How to compare names. `"natural"` treats digits as numbers, so `item2` comes before `item10`. `"line-length"` sorts by the length of the member. `"custom"` sorts by `alphabet`. `"unsorted"` leaves the order alone and only applies `groups`. `"subgroup-order"` sorts by the position of the group inside a nested list in `groups`. |
| `order` | `"asc"` | `"desc"` reverses the order. |
| `ignoreCase` | `true` | Compare names in lower case. |
| `specialCharacters` | `"keep"` | `"trim"` ignores characters other than letters at the start of a name, `"remove"` ignores them everywhere. |
| `alphabet` | `""` | The characters in the order they sort in, for `type: "custom"`. |
| `locales` | `"en-US"` | The locale that `"alphabetical"` and `"natural"` compare names in. |
| `sortBy` | `"name"` | `"value"` compares the types of the properties instead of their names. |
| `fallbackSort` | `{ type: "unsorted", sortBy: "name" }` | How to order two members that the main comparison finds equal: `type`, and optionally `order` and `sortBy`. |
| `groups` | `[]` | The order of the groups. A nested list makes several groups count as one. Members that match no group come last, or where `"unknown"` is. |
| `customGroups` | `[]` | Groups of your own: `{ groupName, elementNamePattern }`, `elementValuePattern`, `selector`, `modifiers`, or `anyOf` with a list of those. A custom group can also carry its own `type`, `order`, `sortBy`, `fallbackSort` and `newlinesInside`. |
| `newlinesBetween` | `"ignore"` | The number of empty lines between groups, `0` for none. A `{ newlinesBetween }` entry in `groups` sets it between two groups. |
| `newlinesInside` | `"newlinesBetween"` | The number of empty lines between two members of the same group, `"ignore"` to leave them alone. The default follows `newlinesBetween`. |
| `partitionByNewLine` | `false` | Sort each block of members that is separated by an empty line on its own. |
| `partitionByComment` | `false` | `true`: a comment between two members separates two blocks that are sorted on their own. A pattern or a list of patterns: only a comment that matches. `{ block, line }`: separately for `/* */` and `//` comments. |
| `useConfigurationIf` | `{}` | When this configuration applies: `allNamesMatchPattern`, `hasNumericKeysOnly`, `declarationMatchesPattern` (the name of the declaration), `declarationCommentMatchesPattern` (the comment above it) or `matchesAstSelector` (an ESLint selector). |

The groups a member can fall in are `"property"`, `"method"` (a method, or a property whose type is a function) and `"index-signature"`, and `"member"` for any of them. In front of one of those you can put `"optional-"` or `"required-"`, and `"multiline-"` for a member that spans several lines, in either order: `"optional-property"`, `"multiline-required-method"`.

### `type`

{/* bad {"options": [{"type": "natural"}]} */}
```ts
interface Sizes {
  item10: string;
  item2: string;
}
```

{/* good {"options": [{"type": "natural"}]} */}
```ts
interface Sizes {
  item2: string;
  item10: string;
}
```

### `groups`

Put required properties first, then optional ones, then methods:

```toml bunfig.toml
[lint.rules]
"perfectionist/sort-interfaces" = ["error", {
  groups = ["required-property", "optional-property", "method"],
}]
```

{/* bad {"options": [{"groups": ["required-property", "optional-property", "method"]}]} */}
```ts
interface User {
  email?: string;
  id: number;
  save(): void;
}
```

{/* good {"options": [{"groups": ["required-property", "optional-property", "method"]}]} */}
```ts
interface User {
  id: number;
  email?: string;
  save(): void;
}
```

### `sortBy`

With `"value"`, the types decide:

{/* bad {"options": [{"sortBy": "value"}]} */}
```ts
interface User {
  id: string;
  age: number;
}
```

{/* good {"options": [{"sortBy": "value"}]} */}
```ts
interface User {
  age: number;
  id: string;
}
```

### `partitionByNewLine` and `partitionByComment`

An empty line or a comment keeps what is above it apart from what is below:

{/* good {"options": [{"partitionByNewLine": true}]} */}
```ts
interface User {
  id: number;
  name: string;

  createdAt: Date;
}
```

{/* good {"options": [{"partitionByComment": true}]} */}
```ts
interface User {
  id: number;
  name: string;
  // Timestamps
  createdAt: Date;
}
```
